problem:
Find a direction vector of the line that is given as the intersection of the following two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x+4z-11=0 \\ x-2y+31=0\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
First, we notice:

- For the plane $-3x+4z-11=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨-3,0,4⟩.$

- For the plane $x-2y+31=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨1,-2,0⟩.$

To find a direction vector for the line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} \\  & =⟨-3,0,4⟩\times ⟨1,-2,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =8i+4j+6k \\  & =⟨8,4,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$
